subject.title: iOS/macOS app cannot connect to a Gateway behind a Basic-auth reverse proxy

question: Should macOS adopt the same arbitrary per-gateway custom-header contract that landed for iOS/Android, or should macOS narrow this issue to typed Basic-auth proxy credentials first?
rationale: The remaining code gap is clear, but the permanent macOS design decides how pre-Gateway proxy credentials are stored, redacted, cleared, and attached before the normal Gateway auth boundary.

options.title: Use the landed custom-header contract
options.body: Add macOS parity for arbitrary sanitized per-gateway headers with Keychain storage, TLS-only request-time injection, reset cleanup, and tests matching the iOS/Android contract.

options.title: Narrow to Basic auth only
options.body: Implement only typed Basic username/password support for macOS, reducing the header surface but diverging from the broader mobile custom-header contract.

options.title: Defer macOS proxy credentials
options.body: Document macOS as unsupported for authenticated reverse-proxy Gateway access until maintainers define a separate desktop credential model.

recommendation.title: Use the landed custom-header contract
recommendation.body: Add macOS parity for arbitrary sanitized per-gateway headers with Keychain storage, TLS-only request-time injection, reset cleanup, and tests matching the iOS/Android contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter owns the landed iOS contract and explicitly identified macOS parity as the remaining issue scope.
